summary: The root مَلَلَ (mll) primarily signifies weariness, boredom, or becoming tired of something. It implies a state of being fed up or disgusted, leading to abandonment or neglect.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: مَلَّهُ He put it (namely bread, or flesh-meat,) into hot ashes, [ to bake, or roast ]. (K, &c.) مَلَّ الثَّوْبَ He sewed, or tacked, the garment, or piece of cloth, [ slightly, ] previously to the [ stronger ] sewing termed الكَفّ. (S.) See also شَلَّ. مَلِلْتُهُ, & مَلِلْتُ عَنْهُ, I was avers from it; (T;) loathed it; was disgusted by it, with it, or at it; (T, S, K;) [ was weary of it; ] turned away from it with disgust. (T.) See سَئِمَ.
أَمْلَلْتُ & أَمْلَيْتُ: see 4 in art. حظ. أَمَلَّ: see an ex. voce أَدَلَّ.
اِمْتَلَّ مِلَّتَهُ He follows his way of religion: see 8 in art. شرع.

مَلَّةٌ The hollow that is made for baking bread: or the hot dust and ashes [ in which the bread is baked ]. (Msb.) Hot ashes: (S, K:) ashes, and earth, in which fire is kindled. (TA, art. خبز.) خُبْزُ مَلَّةٍ Bread baked in hot ashes. (S.) [It is generally made in the form of thick round cakes.]
مِلَّةٌ A religion; (S, Msb, K;) a way of belief and practice in respect of religion. (T, &c.) See 8.
مَلِيلٌ A man burned by the sun; as also. (TA.) See an ex. in a verse cited voce أَصْرَمُ; and see طُلْمَهٌ.
مَمْلُولٌ Flesh-meat covered over in live coals. (TA, art. عرض.) See مَلِيلٌ.

مُلْمُولٌ An iron style with which one writes on tablets. (K.) The style, or bodkin, with which collyrium is applied to the eyes. (S, K.) In the CK, incorrectly, مَلْمُولٌ: the former is found in MS. copies of the K, as well as in the S, and is right accord. to the TK.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
